notes: Sound is the big one. On PCs where the engineer had simply gone quiet, the free online voice was returning audio that Windows never reported a length for, so every single line waited six seconds and then said nothing at all - the app now gives up after four and plays it through a second player instead. If that online voice is down completely, it stops being tried for ninety seconds rather than making every message pay the same wait. The built-in Windows voice had a fault that could take the whole app down on the very first sentence it spoke, which hit anyone running without the downloaded voice and without a cloud key. And if something has pulled the app down to one percent in the Windows volume mixer, the app now puts itself back up. When sound still fails, the error report finally says which output device is default, whether Windows will open it, and how loud the app is allowed to be. Test radio no longer prints text and stays silent when the engineer voice box is unticked - it now tells you that is why. iRacing: if the sim is running as administrator the app cannot read it, and it used to just say iRacing starting forever, even while you were driving - it now recognises exactly that and tells you to start PitWise as administrator too. The microphone got a measured pass rather than a guessed one: quiet speech that transcribes perfectly well is no longer thrown away, the loudness reading is taken from the whole recording instead of the first loud moment, a whisper server that answers with an error is no longer treated as one that simply heard nothing, recording falls back through other formats and other microphones instead of sticking to one that only records silence, a headset plugged in while the app is open now appears in the list, and the engineer no longer answers things you never said, because the transcriber inventing sounds like music or a website address is filtered out. Corner data has been rebuilt from the community source: 442 tracks instead of 222, and the right layout is now picked by track length, so Spa with its thirteen recorded versions cannot land on the wrong one. The Nordschleife 24h layout finally has its 49 named corners rather than 14 guessed from speed, and lap history now names corners in its headings, so it reads T7 Bruxelles rather than just T7. Lap Times has a new Ideal line: the lap you would have done from your best sector times this session, with how much it is worth against your best actual lap. The radio is laid out as text messages, the engineer on one side and you on the other, so a conversation reads as a conversation. You can set two names in Settings: the nickname shown on setups you share, and the name the engineer calls you on the radio - both optional, both translated into 27 languages, and shared setups no longer record which country they came from. Le Mans Ultimate and rF2: the spotter worked out left and right from a value the plugin itself documents as very approximate, and now uses the car orientation instead, and the track map was being drawn mirrored, so left corners appeared as right ones - laps you recorded before this will still be mirrored until you drive the track again. When Google answers the engineer with the model is busy, try again, the app now tries again twice instead of dropping straight to its offline answer. Most of this was verified by reading the code, on your own stored laps and in demo mode rather than out on track, so if the engineer says something odd out there, please use the feedback form in the app.
